advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Distinguish an explicit operator step budget of 250 from the unset default at completion.py:587 (e.g. thread an 'explicitly set' flag) so lever-1 never lowers a budget the operator actually chose.
evidence: completion.py:587 `if cfg.max_iterations == DEFAULT_MAX_ITERATIONS or cfg.max_iterations < step_floor:`
config.py:125-126 comment: 'An operator can still lower it via REBAR_LLM_MAX_STEPS' — so an operator explicitly choosing 250 is a real input, yet it is indistinguishable from the unset default here
completion.py:558-560 docstring claims it is 'min-only against an EXPLICIT operator budget (a different value the operator set is only ever raised up to the floor, never lowered)'
advisory.finding: Lever-1 step-floor apply site treats an operator budget that happens to equal DEFAULT_MAX_ITERATIONS (250) as 'no explicit budget' and LOWERS it to the criteria-scaled floor, contradicting the documented min-only 'explicit operator budget still wins' contract.
scenarios: An operator sets REBAR_LLM_MAX_STEPS=250 intending a 250-step budget on a small (e.g. 2-criterion) ticket; the code sees max_iterations==250==DEFAULT and replaces it with the scaled floor (48), silently lowering the budget below what the operator asked for.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Update diag_runaway_matrix.py:95 to drive the step floor via the new mechanism (verify_step_floor config / REBAR_LLM_MAX_STEPS) instead of the removed `_VERIFY_MIN_STEPS`.
evidence: completion.py now only defines `_VERIFY_STEP_FLOOR_MAX` and reads it: src/rebar/llm/completion.py:91 `_VERIFY_STEP_FLOOR_MAX = 480`, :105 `return max(lo, min(scaled, _VERIFY_STEP_FLOOR_MAX))`
advisory.finding: diag_runaway_matrix.py sets `_completion._VERIFY_MIN_STEPS = floor`, but `_VERIFY_MIN_STEPS` was removed from completion.py (renamed to `_VERIFY_STEP_FLOOR_MAX` + `verify_step_floor()`), so the assignment creates a dead attribute the module never reads — the intended step-floor lowering is a silent no-op.
scenarios: Running the matrix diagnostic to force cheap bounded runs at floors 50/240/480 — the floor override has no effect on the actual step budget.
advisory.suggested_fix: Set `os.environ["REBAR_LLM_MAX_STEPS"]` (already done) and, if a hard cap is needed, patch `_completion._VERIFY_STEP_FLOOR_MAX` and/or the VerifyConfig `completion_verify_step_floor_min`/`completion_verify_steps_per_criterion` fields rather than the removed `_VERIFY_MIN_STEPS`.

evidence: completion.py now sizes the budget via `verify_step_floor(criteria_count, verify_cfg)` (src/rebar/llm/completion.py:585) and no longer reads `_VERIFY_MIN_STEPS`
advisory.finding: diag_runaway_transcript.py sets `_completion._VERIFY_MIN_STEPS = floor`, but `_VERIFY_MIN_STEPS` was removed from completion.py, so the 'induced exhaustion' step-floor override is a dead assignment the module ignores.
scenarios: Running the transcript diagnostic expecting a cheap bounded run at floor=50 — the floor override silently does nothing.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the 50 vs 250 framework-default numbers in the completion.py step-floor comment block.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/completion.py: 'The framework review default (REBAR_LLM_MAX_STEPS=50 ≈ 25 tool calls) is far too low'
src/rebar/llm/completion.py: 'it may LOWER a small ticket below the 250 default — that is the point'
dropped.finding: The completion.py step-floor comment block contradicts itself on the framework default step budget: it states the framework review default is `REBAR_LLM_MAX_STEPS=50 ≈ 25 tool calls` but a later comment in the same block says the criteria-scaled floor 'may LOWER a small ticket below the 250 default'.
scenarios: A reader reconciling the two comments cannot tell whether the framework default budget is 50 or 250 steps.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Prefer exact model equality (and only fall back to a bounded, unambiguous match) in resolve_verifier_slot so overlapping model names cannot mis-resolve the class slot.
evidence: completion_banking.py:245 `if model and (resolved == model or (slot_model and slot_model in model)):`
The first CLASS_NAMES entry whose slot_model is a substring of `model` wins, so ordering + substring overlap decides the slot rather than an exact model identity
dropped.finding: resolve_verifier_slot matches a slot by substring (`slot_model in model`), which can misclassify the verifier's class slot when configured model strings overlap (e.g. a 'standard' slot model that is a substring of the resolved frontier model), yielding the wrong successor batch cap.
scenarios: Two configured slot models where one is a substring of the other (or of the resolved model) cause the wrong slot (and thus batch cap 8 vs 12) to be selected.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm/handle the exactly-_READ_MAX_LINES boundary so a complete cap-length file is still served from cache (e.g. detect EOF vs cap explicitly) rather than always falling back.
evidence: pai_tools.py:64 read_file caps `hi = min(hi, lo + _READ_MAX_LINES - 1)` so a file of exactly 2000 lines returns 2000 rows and is indistinguishable from a >2000-line file at line 227
dropped.finding: The path-normalized read_file cache marks a file whose whole-file read returns exactly _READ_MAX_LINES rows as truncated (complete=False), so a complete file of exactly the cap length forces a fallback exact-range read on every subsequent read rather than serving from cache.
scenarios: A source file of exactly 2000 lines: repeated reads bypass the cache (complete=False and no explicit line_end<=2000), re-billing the provider — the exact re-read waste lever 2 targets.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a recovery-orchestration test with a successor stub whose _usage reports substantial actual spend, asserting the next batched run's iteration_limit/budget reflects the reduced pool_remaining (and that spend > budget is clamped).
evidence: All recovery successor stubs report _usage requests of 0 or 1 (test_completion_banking.py lines 336/362/384/404/428; test_completion_token_recovery.py:107/245; test_completion_recovery_*), so pool_remaining barely changes between batches — the min(spent, budget) clamp and unspent-budget inheritance for a later run are never verified against real spend.
dropped.finding: The live successor re-planning that budgets from ACTUAL spend (allocate_batch + pool_remaining = max(0, pool_remaining - min(spent, budget)) in completion_recovery._run_successors) is never exercised with a successor that actually spends a meaningful fraction of its allocated budget: every recovery-orchestration stub returns _usage requests of 0 or 1. A regression in the actual-spend clamp or in the pool inheritance that shrinks a later batched run's allocation would go undetected — the multi-batch test (test_no_per_criterion_fan_out) launches two batches but with requests=0 each, so the second batch's allocation is indistinguishable from a static plan.
scenarios: A successor consumes most of its allocated request budget, shrinking pool_remaining so a subsequent batch is planned at a smaller (or zero) allocation.
A regression that drops the min(spent, budget) clamp or mis-computes pool inheritance across two live batched successor runs.
